idiom_name: validating receiver + dedicated invalid channel + error-handling consumer (declared as topology)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: every receiver validates before it acts - framing and decode checks, schema and mandatory-field checks, then business-rule checks - and has exactly one defined action for a failure: move the untouched message to the invalid channel and only then acknowledge the original. The channel is declared as topology (a queue or topic, an exchange binding, a dead-letter policy, or a failed set) and is never used for normal traffic; an error handler consumes it, stores the frame with its reason, source channel, sender and correlation id, and drives repair, replay or discard. Keep the classification explicit: deterministic invalidity goes to the invalid channel, transient failure to retry, undeliverable messages to the dead-letter channel. Bound depth and retention and alert on growth, or the channel becomes an unmonitored dumping ground.
code_sketch:
receive(msg)
if not valid(msg):
    invalid_channel.publish(raw(msg), reason=why, source=channel, cid=msg.id)
    ack(msg)                      # only after the diverted copy is durable
    return
process(decode(msg)); ack(msg)
pitfalls: Acknowledging before the invalid copy is durably accepted loses the only evidence of the defect.
One shared invalid channel for unrelated senders, without correlation metadata, makes diagnosis guesswork.
Routing every failure - including transient ones - to the invalid channel floods it and hides the genuinely malformed messages.
Re-serializing the decoded envelope before diverting destroys the evidence (unknown fields, wrong types, truncated frames).

Wrong move: Treat a broker dead-letter reason as proof that the payload is invalid -> delivery-limit or TTL events can represent retry-policy exhaustion or stale-but-well-formed data, sending recoverable work to quarantine -> instead inspect validation results and broker reason separately before choosing retry, expiration, or invalid-message routing.

Wrong move: Blindly replay every quarantined message after a deployment -> duplicate side effects or a still-poisoned batch can re-enter the live path -> instead require idempotency, authenticated operator approval, and bounded replay batches with a kill switch.

Wrong move: Let the invalid channel inherit primary-queue retention and access defaults -> sensitive payloads remain indefinitely or become broadly readable -> instead set explicit TTL, encryption, least-privilege access, and an auditable purge path.
